interest: Offers rare legal treatises and government surveys detailing post-WWII Japanese nationality, Nisei dual citizenship, and imperial territorial dismantlement.
overview: This file documents the legal framework, administrative policies, and diplomatic challenges surrounding Japanese citizenship, nationality recovery, and personal status during the Allied occupation from 1945 to 1949. Central matters include statutory analyses of Japanese nationality legislation dating back to 1899, administrative procedures for renouncing and restoring citizenship, and dual nationality questions concerning American-born Nisei and Anglo-Japanese individuals. The records feature significant legal monographs—notably by Thomas L. Blakemore—alongside SCAP directives regarding travel documents, blank renunciation forms, specific citizenship determinations and court evidence, and comprehensive Japanese government studies on post-war repatriation, demographics, and the civil status of populations in detached imperial territories like Formosa, Korea, Saghalien, and the Kuriles.
